claims.text: First-principles DFT calculations can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys in low-dimensional applications.
First-principles DFT calculations can be used to tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys in low-dimensional applications.
DFT can predict how compositional adjustments modify the electronic structure of non-equiatomic HEAs.
DFT can predict how compositional adjustments modify the magnetic moments of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Composition-driven modulation of electronic structure and magnetic moments can produce enhanced or tailored magnetic properties.
Composition-driven modulation of electronic structure and magnetic moments can produce enhanced or tailored magnetocaloric properties.
DFT has limitations in accurately predicting the behavior of complex, non-equiatomic HEA systems.
Experimental magnetic moments and magnetocaloric effects can be compared with DFT predictions to test the proposed tuning method.
The hypothesis is falsified if experimental magnetic and magnetocaloric properties correlate with DFT predictions for fewer than 75% of tested compositions.
